name: Mebeverine

overview.mechanism: Used to relieve intestinal spasms; clinical studies assess symptomatic benefit in irritable bowel syndrome. [[MEB-D,MEB-PC]]
uses: Symptomatic treatment studied in irritable bowel syndrome; verify the indication and formulation-specific instructions for the local product. [[MEB-D,MEB-PC]]

paragraphs.text: In a 40-patient, eight-week randomized study of controlled-release mebeverine in diarrhea-predominant IBS, abdominal cramps, bowel-movement frequency and quality of life improved within the mebeverine group. However, between-group differences versus placebo were not significant. Improvement from baseline alone therefore does not establish drug efficacy. Both groups were described as well tolerated.

An exploratory primary-care factorial trial enrolled 135 patients and compared mebeverine, methylcellulose and placebo alongside website interventions. IBS symptom-severity and quality-of-life outcomes did not differ significantly between medication groups at six or twelve weeks. The feasibility design and sample size limit definitive conclusions.

These IBS trials were not renal pharmacokinetic or dialysis studies. Their short-term tolerability findings do not establish safety in advanced CKD or a renal dosing schedule. Formulation-specific contraindications, hypersensitivity precautions and current local prescribing information still require verification.

sources.citation: Will controlled release mebeverine be able to surpass placebo in treatment of diarrhoea predominant irritable bowel syndrome? PubMed PMID: 31742138.

Management of irritable bowel syndrome in primary care: results of an exploratory randomised controlled trial of mebeverine, methylcellulose, placebo and a self-management website. PubMed PMID: 23602047.

draft_notes: No dose recommendations added; local label, renal impairment, allergy and formulation-specific prescribing details remain gaps.

renal: The cited clinical studies do not establish a renal adjustment or dialysis regimen; product-specific prescribing information remains to be verified [[MEB-D,MEB-PC]].

common: Both groups were described as well tolerated in the small IBS-D trial; this is limited short-term evidence and not a comprehensive adverse-reaction inventory [[MEB-D]].
